text:
mia.security: quick follow-up from the RFC meeting — thinking through operator token pinning for multi-tenant flows. want to capture tradeoffs and a migration sketch.
ken.platform: tl;dr? are we talking short-lived tokens the operator mints and hands to services, or pinning long-lived operator credentials?
sam.infra: we landed on short TTLs in the meeting but some teams asked for pinning for affinity/perf. that's what we need to weigh.
mia.security: right. two concrete options: (A) operator mints ephemeral scoped tokens per request (TTL ~1m), keep them opaque and revocable; (B) operator issues pinned session tokens per tenant (TTL ~24h) to reduce handshake cost.
olivia.prodsec: security-first: ephemeral tokens are obviously better for blast-radius. but perf and downstream rate limits matter.
ken.platform: performance: the hot path is operator -> gpu-proxy -> model-host. extra minting per call adds CPU + KMS ops. We could cache per-tenant token in proxy for 1m windows, but then revocation is delayed.
sam.infra: revocation semantics are important: with opaque tokens we can revoke centrally and proxies must check introspect on miss. with pinned tokens we need a revocation list or short TTL. revocation list scales badly.
mia.security: suggestion: hybrid: issue pinned short-lived tokens (TTL 15m) and enable immediate revocation via a lightweight invalidation pubsub to proxies. that reduces mint ops but keeps revocation timely.
ken.platform: 15m still feels long for some compliance teams. can we make TTL configurable per-tenant? e.g., default 5m, allow enterprise tenants to request up to 24h with contract and enhanced monitoring.
olivia.prodsec: yes, configurable TTL per tenant + contract gating is OK. require additional audit trail and HSM-backed signing for long-lived.
sam.infra: implementation notes: proxies should keep token cache with LRU and TTL, and subscribe to an invalidation channel: 
```
# pseudo-config
token_cache:
  ttl: 900 # seconds
  max_entries: 10000
invalidation_topic: ops/auth/invalidate
```

sam.infra: on invalidation message we evict matching tenant keys. invalidate messages should be compact (tenant_id + token_id).
ken.platform: how do we represent scope in the token? tenant-only, or tenant+capabilities? capability claims allow least privilege but make rollout harder.
mia.security: prefer tenant+capabilities in claims. keep a narrow capability vocabulary (generate, read-embeddings, admin) and version it. tokens carry capability_set_id. if capability vocab changes, operator denies old capability_set_ids.
olivia.prodsec: audit: every mint and revocation must be logged to immutable audit store and surfaced in console with token_id, tenant_id, issuer, ttl, capabilities. retention policy for long-lived tokens must be explicit.
ken.platform: migration plan? many services still expect static API keys today.
mia.security: plan sketch: 1) pilot: opt-in tenants use pinning hybrid with 15m TTL + invalidation. 2) instrument latencies and KMS ops. 3) enable default short TTLs (1m) across platform. 4) deprecate static keys: provide import/export shim for a transition window and rotate.
sam.infra: operational checks: measure token-mint QPS, KMS request rate, cache hit ratio. set autoscale triggers.
olivia.prodsec: policy: forbid granting admin capability via pinned tokens unless explicit approval.
deploy-bot: :rocket: deployed auth-invalidation-service v0.2 to staging (build #2024-13)
ken.platform: nice. next up: proof-of-concept for invalidation pubsub and proxy cache eviction. can volunteer to pair with infra on that.
mia.security: awesome — ken + sam pair and ping me for policy UI hooks. i'll draft a short RFC addendum with the hybrid TTL defaults and migration timeline. :thumbsup:
